text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card and the leaning of 'inconclusive' agrees with the hybrid_review. The next steps are sensible. But the headline '30/30 charts support billing' overstates the evidence: only 5 of the 30 charts were for 99215 claims, and only 30 of 955 claims were documented. The headline also conflicts with the body, which calls the records too thin to judge. The cited examples are two zero-condition 99215 claims, which fit the low-complexity point but are thin. The summary leaves out the 10 high-complexity claims and the by-complexity gradient. It does not mention the documented 99215 examples with high MDM. 'Statistical outlier only' is a bit conclusory.","problems":["Headline '30/30 charts support billing' is misleading: only 5 documented 99215 claims, and none were below billed level does not mean all charts support the billed level; it contradicts the 'too thin to judge' next step.","Only two example claims cited, both 0-condition cases; the card offers 25 low-complexity claims, so the evidence is thin.","Headline leads with 'z_adj 8.9' jargon rather than a clear statement of the finding (17.5% vs 3.1% expected 99215).","Does not mention the complexity gradient (99215 share rising with conditions) or that 66% of 99215s were on higher-complexity patients, which tempers the concern.","Next steps are generic and do not name specific claims to request records for, and the sample size is unspecified."]}
